The round‑trip time of the light is  

\[
t=\frac{2D}{c}
\]

and the wheel must rotate by the angular width of one gap during this time.  
With \(N\) teeth there are \(N\) gaps, so the angular spacing of a gap is \(\frac{1}{2N}\) of a revolution.  
Hence  

\[
t=\frac{1}{2N\,f}\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 
c=4D\,N\,f .
\]

Using \(D=4980\;\text{m},\; N=600\) and the first extinction at \(f=1500\;\text{rpm}=25\;\text{Hz}\),

\[
c = 4(4980)(600)(25)=2.99\times10^{8}\ \text{m s}^{-1},
\]

which agrees with the accepted value.  
For the second extinction the wheel must rotate by two gap widths, i.e. twice the angular displacement of the first case, so the required frequency is twice the first one:

\[
f_{2}=2f_{1}=2\times1500\;\text{rpm}=3000\;\text{rpm}.
\]

The answer that provides the correct speed of light and the appropriate higher rotation rate is option **G**.
